name: Gettysburg Battlefield
description: Site of the July 1–3, 1863 Battle of Gettysburg, the bloodiest engagement of the American Civil War. The battlefield and adjacent town are among the most extensively reported haunted locations in the United States, with ghost lore dating back to the immediate aftermath of the battle and a major commercial ghost-tour industry from the 1990s onward.
full_description: The Gettysburg Battlefield, in Adams County, Pennsylvania, is the site of the three-day Battle of Gettysburg (July 1–3, 1863), the deadliest battle of the American Civil War. Combined casualty estimates range from 46,000 to 51,000 killed, wounded, captured, or missing. Confederate General Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia was repulsed by Union Major General George G. Meade's Army of the Potomac, and the battle is widely regarded as the war's turning point. Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, delivered at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery on November 19, 1863, secured the battlefield's place in American memory. The site became Gettysburg National Military Park in 1895, and is now operated by the National Park Service. Alongside its historical significance, Gettysburg is one of the most-cited haunted locations in the United States. Ghost stories are documented from the immediate post-battle period, when townspeople and burial details described unusual sounds and apparitions, and have continued to multiply since. Specific paranormal traditions cluster at Devil's Den, the Triangular Field, Little Round Top, the Wheatfield, Sachs Bridge, the Jennie Wade House (where the only documented civilian killed in the battle, Mary Virginia 'Jennie' Wade, was struck by a stray bullet on July 3, 1863), the Daniel Lady Farm, and the Farnsworth House Inn. Mark Nesbitt, a former park ranger, published the first volume of his 'Ghosts of Gettysburg' series in 1991 and founded the Ghosts of Gettysburg Candlelight Walking Tours in 1994, helping anchor the modern ghost-tourism industry. Mainstream historians and the National Park Service treat the ghost stories as folklore.

aliases.name: Ghosts of Gettysburg
aliases.meaning: popular name for the cluster of paranormal traditions associated with the battlefield

origin: Reports are concentrated within the roughly 6,000-acre Gettysburg National Military Park, the borough of Gettysburg, and immediately surrounding farmland in Adams County, Pennsylvania.

etymology.origin: The town of Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, was named for early settler James Gettys (founded 1786). The 'Ghosts of Gettysburg' phrase was popularized by Mark Nesbitt's book series beginning in 1991.
etymology.meaning: Gettysburg = town of the Gettys family
